This is Cascade Legal Rights Project. Thank you to the moderator for inviting us to respond, and to everyone who raised this.

We understand why people are upset. Getting a letter from a law firm right after you've asked for help is scary, and it's fair to wonder how they got your name. You deserve a plain answer.

We do not share, sell or disclose information about the people who come to our clinics. Our policy prohibits it, and it specifically bars giving attendee information to landlords or their attorneys. Sign-in records stay inside our organization and are kept in locked storage.

Here is what we think is the most likely explanation for the letters. When a landlord files an eviction case in magistrate court, that filing is a public record. Some law firms use those filings to get tenants' names and addresses and send them mailings. That means someone with a case filed against them can get one of these letters whether or not they have ever spoken to us.

We won't discuss any individual's situation on this board, because that is exactly the kind of privacy we're promising to protect. If you received a letter and want to talk it through, or you have questions about how we handle your information, please contact us directly and we'll go over it with you.

The clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10am to 1pm, and everyone is welcome. One change: the library's meeting room is closed that day for repairs, so we'll be at the Mt Zion fellowship hall in East Atlanta instead. The side entrance by the parking lot is accessible. As before, it's free and walk-in, with no appointment needed. Volunteer attorneys and staff will be there to look at eviction notices and court papers and explain your options.

If you have doubts, come and ask us in person. We'd rather hear the hard questions than have anyone go without help because they were afraid to come.

Questions: clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187.
